name: Open-interest expansion + band breakout — leverage-backed breakout (spot long)
rationale: MECHANISM (why OI leads the breakout): a breakout on rising open_interest means NEW leveraged capital is opening into the move — fresh money committing, the fuel a breakout needs to hold. A band breakout on FLAT or falling OI is short-covering or thin spot churn that fades back inside the range. OI (perp-derived) reveals whether the marginal breakout buyer is real leverage or a hollow print, and it builds INTO the breakout bar. We require open_interest above a fitted (normalized) floor AND bb_z above a breakout threshold (a statistically unusual push through the upper band), then ride it, exiting when bb_z falls back to the mean (breakout failed). Distinct from OI-confirmed-momentum (ret_Nd): this triggers on a VOLATILITY-band breakout, not a smooth return. DISCONFIRMER 1: if the bb_z breakout alone (no OI arm) matches the deflated Sharpe, OI adds nothing. DISCONFIRMER 2: OI co-moves with price, so if an OI-falling arm does as well, OI is a price proxy, not a leverage-flow signal.
catalyst: open_interest is expanding (new leverage entering) AND price breaks ABOVE its Bollinger band (bb_z high).
